findings.evidence: eval_adapter.py:1114-1117 uses `finditer(r"^\s*#\s+(invariant|fast) ...", wf, re.M)` over the whole file, while ADR-019 §5:242-243 says the comparison is against the copy in eval.yml's comment block. findings.acceptance: Either the parse is scoped to the comment region preceding the `EVAL_WALL_BUDGET_S_*` env block, or §5 stops saying 'comment block' and says 'a comment in .github/workflows/eval.yml'.

findings.claim: The newly load-bearing third copy has no one-band rule: a second, contradictory `# invariant ...` comment placed BEFORE the real one in eval.yml leaves the gate green, because the dict comprehension keeps the last match.
findings.evidence: eval_adapter.py:1114-1117 — `wf_cells = {m[1]: [...] for m in finditer(...)}`. Inserting a contradictory line immediately ABOVE eval.yml:24 gives passed True; inserting the same line immediately BELOW gives red with `{workflow_comment: [11.11, 22.22, 33.33, 44.44]}`. This is exactly T-R51's 'Compounding' clause — one document publishing the CI band twice, incompatibly — which `publishes_more_than_one_ci_band` refuses in README, now reproducible in the workflow, the document round 3 promoted to a graded source. Neither §5 nor the triage note claims the workflow is one-band-only, so this is an unstated gap rather than a false claim.
findings.repro: insert a contradictory `# invariant ...` line above eval.yml:24 -> passed True
findings.acceptance: Either duplicate suite lines in the workflow are refused, matching README's one-band rule, or the triage note names 'a second contradictory band inside the workflow' in its NOT-covered list.
